# share.mk

> Anonymous, zero-signup file sharing with automatic expiry. No account needed. Files are stored on S3 (Scaleway) and deleted automatically when they expire.

## Quick start for AI assistants

The easiest way to share a file from an AI assistant is the built-in MCP (Model Context Protocol) server.

MCP endpoint (Streamable HTTP): https://share.mk/mcp

### MCP tools

**upload_file** — Upload a file and get back links to share

Parameters:
- filename (required): original filename, e.g. "report.pdf"
- content (required): base64-encoded file content (standard or URL-safe encoding)
- content_type (optional): MIME type, e.g. "application/pdf" — defaults to application/octet-stream.
  Set it correctly: it decides whether the link previews in the browser.
- expires_in (optional): 1h | 6h | 24h | 7d | 30d — defaults to 24h
- password (optional): password required to open the file. Share it separately from the link.
- disposition (optional): "inline" (default) or "attachment". "attachment" never previews the file:
  browsers get a download page, other clients get the file as an attachment.

Returns:
{ "file_id", "management_token", "manage_url", "download_url", "direct_download_url",
  "expires_at", "filename", "size_bytes", "password_protected" }

- download_url — the link to share (https://share.mk/files/{objectId}/{filename}). Opens in the browser
  for previewable files; otherwise shows a page with the filename, size, expiry and a Download button.
- direct_download_url — always downloads (https://share.mk/dl/{objectId}/{filename}).
- manage_url — web page where the uploader can view and delete the file.

IMPORTANT: Save the management_token (or manage_url). It is returned only once and is required for
get_file_info and delete_file. Nobody else needs it to download the file.

Size limit: MCP requests are capped at 16 MiB, which is about 12 MB of file content after base64
encoding. For larger files use the REST (tus) upload below.

---

**get_file_info** — Look up an uploaded file

Parameters:
- file_id (required): the file_id returned by upload_file
- management_token (required): the token returned by upload_file

Returns:
{ "file_id", "filename", "content_type", "size_bytes", "complete", "download_url",
  "direct_download_url", "expires_at", "disposition", "password_protected" }

---

**delete_file** — Permanently delete an uploaded file before it expires

Parameters:
- file_id (required): the file_id returned by upload_file
- management_token (required): the token returned by upload_file

Returns: { "deleted": true, "file_id" }

---

## REST API

Interactive docs: https://share.mk/docs
OpenAPI 3.1 spec: https://share.mk/openapi.json

Uploads use the tus resumable upload protocol (https://tus.io): create the upload with POST,
send the bytes with PATCH, resume after interruptions by reading the offset with HEAD.

### Upload-Metadata header

Comma-separated `key base64(value)` pairs:

- filename — original filename
- filetype — MIME type
- expires-in — 1h, 6h, 24h (default), 7d, 30d
- password — optional download password (only a hash is stored)
- disposition — optional: inline (default) or attachment

Invalid values are rejected with 400 and no upload is created.

The 201 response headers:
- Location — tus upload URL for PATCH/HEAD
- Upload-Share-URL — the link to share (https://share.mk/files/{objectId}/{filename})
- Upload-Management-Token — secret token, shown only once; keep it to delete the file early
- Upload-Manage-URL — web page to view and delete the file (token in the URL fragment)

### Example (curl)

```bash
# 1. Create the upload
curl -D - -X POST https://share.mk/files/ \
  -H "Tus-Resumable: 1.0.0" \
  -H "Upload-Length: $(wc -c < report.pdf)" \
  -H "Upload-Metadata: filename $(printf report.pdf | base64),filetype $(printf application/pdf | base64),expires-in $(printf 7d | base64)"
# → Location: https://share.mk/files/{id}
# → Upload-Share-URL: https://share.mk/files/{objectId}/report.pdf
# → Upload-Management-Token: {token}

# 2. Send the bytes
curl -X PATCH "https://share.mk/files/{id}" \
  -H "Tus-Resumable: 1.0.0" \
  -H "Upload-Offset: 0" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/offset+octet-stream" \
  --data-binary @report.pdf

# 3. Download (curl always receives the file itself)
curl -o report.pdf https://share.mk/files/{objectId}/report.pdf

# 4. File info / delete early
curl https://share.mk/api/files/{id} -H "Authorization: Bearer {token}"
curl -X DELETE https://share.mk/api/files/{id} -H "Authorization: Bearer {token}"
```

`{id}` can be the object ID from the share link or the full ID from Location.

### Links and how files open

- https://share.mk/files/{objectId}/{filename} — share link. The filename part is cosmetic.
  - Images, video (with seeking), audio and PDF open in the browser.
  - Text, HTML, SVG source and code are shown as plain text (UTF-8), never executed.
  - Other files (and uploads with disposition=attachment): browsers get a page with the filename,
    size, expiry and a Download button; non-browser clients (curl, scripts, AI tools) get the bytes.
- https://share.mk/dl/{objectId}/{filename} — always downloads. Adding ?dl=1 to any link does the same.
- Deleted files return 404 (an HTML "File not available" page in browsers). Expired files are
  removed within about 10 minutes of their expiry time.

### Password-protected files

- Browsers get a password form; after unlocking, the file stays open in that browser for 12 hours.
- API clients send the password with HTTP Basic auth (any username):
  curl -u :secret -o file.zip https://share.mk/dl/{objectId}/file.zip

### Management API

Authenticate with the management token: `Authorization: Bearer {token}`.

- GET /api/files/{id} — file info (same fields as get_file_info)
- DELETE /api/files/{id} — delete the file (also aborts an unfinished upload)
- DELETE /files/{id} — same, for tus clients (the token may also go in the Upload-Management-Token header)

## Limits

- Max file size: 10 GiB (tus); about 12 MB via MCP
- Expiry options: 1h, 6h, 24h (default), 7d, 30d
- Concurrent uploads: 5 per IP, 50 overall (HTTP 429 when exceeded)
- MCP: 2 concurrent requests per IP, 10 overall
- Unfinished uploads idle for 48 hours are removed
